draft.title: Resilience and change
card: A disturbance is an event that changes an ecosystem, such as a fire, a drought, a flood or the arrival of a pest. Some are natural and some are caused by people.
the ability of an ecosystem to absorb a disturbance and then recover its main features and functions. Many Australian eucalypt forests regrow after a bushfire.
a threshold where change becomes too great. Past it, the ecosystem shifts to a different state and may not return to how it was, even if the disturbance stops.
Repeated or very severe disturbance, or several pressures at once, can use up resilience. This makes a tipping point more likely to be reached.
draft.remember: Ecosystems can recover from some disturbance, but past a tipping point they may settle into a new state.

a.q: What does it mean to say an ecosystem is resilient?
opts: It can absorb a disturbance and then recover
It never changes when a disturbance occurs
It has already passed a tipping point
It is free from any natural disturbance
a.why: Resilience is the ability to absorb a disturbance and recover. It does not mean the ecosystem is unaffected, because most resilient ecosystems change for a time before they recover.
a.clue: Think about what happens after the disturbance, not during it.

b.q: A woodland in New South Wales burns in a bushfire and regrows within a few years. After repeated fires, drought and grazing by feral animals, it becomes open grassland that does not return to woodland. What best explains this change?
opts: Combined pressures used up resilience and crossed a tipping point
A single bushfire is always enough to destroy a woodland
Resilience means a woodland never changes after a fire
Natural disturbances cannot affect an ecosystem's state
b.why: The woodland recovered from one fire, so it was resilient at first. Repeated fires, drought and grazing together used up that resilience and pushed it past a tipping point into a new state. The idea that one fire destroys a woodland is wrong, as the first regrowth shows.
b.clue: The woodland recovered the first time. What changed after that?

problems.detail: Every wrong option uses an absolute word: 'cannot', 'never' or 'always'. The right option is the only one without one, so a student can pick it by ruling out the absolutes without understanding resilience or tipping points.
The question is very easy for Year 12 HSC. 'Never changes' and 'free from any natural disturbance' are plainly wrong, so it barely tests the idea.

proposal.remember: Ecosystems can recover from some disturbance, but past a tipping point they may settle into a new state.

a.q: A wetland dries out in a long drought. Which outcome would show it was resilient, rather than pushed past a tipping point?
opts: Its plants and birds return once rains refill it
It turns into dry grassland that stays after rain
Its wetland plants are slowly replaced by shrubs
It loses the main features it had before the drought
a.why: A resilient ecosystem absorbs a disturbance and then recovers its main features, so the returning plants and birds show resilience. Grassland that stays after the rain returns is a shift to a new state, which is what happens past a tipping point.
a.clue: Does the wetland end up as it was, or as something else?

b.q: A woodland in New South Wales burns in a bushfire and regrows within a few years. After repeated fires, drought and grazing by feral animals, it becomes open grassland that does not return to woodland. What best explains this change?
opts: Several pressures wore down resilience past a tipping point
The first bushfire pushed the woodland past a tipping point
The woodland grew more resilient with each fire it survived
The grassland is the woodland recovering from the fires
b.why: The woodland regrew after the first fire, so it was resilient then and had not passed a tipping point. Repeated fires, drought and grazing together used up that resilience and pushed it into a new state. The grassland is not recovery, because recovery means the woodland's main features return.
b.clue: The woodland recovered the first time. What changed after that?
